data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      flat: Flat (e.g. Overflow menus)
      sections: Sections (e.g. Google Docs menus)
      cascading-submenus: Cascading submenus (e.g. Desktop menu bars)
      mega-menu: Mega menu — Multi-column panel (e.g. Retail department menus)
* Item content [content] — What does each item show?
  - item (multi-select: list of ids) — Item content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Google Docs)
      shortcut-hint: Shortcut hint (e.g. macOS menus)
      checkmark-state: Checkmark state (e.g. View menus)
      description: Description (e.g. GitHub menus)
* Item set [initiative] — Who decides which items appear and in what order?
  - itemSet (single-select: one id) — Item set
      fixed: Fixed (e.g. Most menus)
      depends-on-selection: Depends on selection (e.g. Context menus)
      adaptive: Adaptive — The system reorders by use (e.g. Office 2000 personalized menus)
      adaptable: Adaptable — The person reorders (e.g. Office Quick Access Toolbar)
* Form [layout] — What shape is it?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      vertical-list: Vertical list (e.g. Most menus)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Blender pie menus)
      icon-grid: Icon grid (e.g. Google apps launcher)
      horizontal-bar: Horizontal bar (e.g. Toolbars)

## card — Card (component, archetype browse-collections)
A bounded container that summarizes one item; the most common item view inside overviews.
Aliases: tile, item card
Anatomy: Media (Image or video); Header (Title and subtitle); Body (Key attributes); Actions (What can be done to the item)
Related — uses: badge, menu | neighbors: stat-tile
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Card content [content] — What goes on the card?
  - media (single-select: one id) — Media
      none: None (e.g. Linear issue cards)
      top-image: Top image (e.g. Airbnb listings)
      side-thumbnail: Side thumbnail (e.g. Spotify search results)
      full-bleed-background: Full-bleed background (e.g. App Store Today cards)
  - actions (single-select: one id) — Actions
      none: None — The card only opens (e.g. News cards)
      one-primary-action: One primary action (e.g. Add to cart on a product card)
      action-row: Action row (e.g. Social post actions)
      overflow-menu: Overflow menu (e.g. Google Drive file cards)
* Form [layout] — What shape and weight does the card take?
  - shape (single-select: one id) — Shape
      vertical: Vertical (e.g. Product grids)
      horizontal: Horizontal (e.g. Search result rows)
      compact-tile: Compact tile (e.g. Home screen widgets)
  - style (single-select: one id) — Container style
      elevated: Elevated (e.g. Material 3 elevated card)
      filled: Filled (e.g. Material 3 filled card)
      outlined: Outlined (e.g. Material 3 outlined card)
      borderless: Borderless — No container at all: no fill, no border and no shadow — the media and text sit directly on the page background and the card is defined only by its grouping and spacing. The default for most modern consumer overviews, and not expressible with Material's three container styles (e.g. Airbnb — Listing card in

data.name: search_codebook
data.text:
tabs (component · navigate) — Tabs: A set of peer views sharing one space, one visible at a time, switched by labelled controls. [aka tab bar, segmented control, tab strip]
carousel (component · browse-collections) — Carousel: A horizontally scrolling strip that shows a subset of items at once and hides the rest off-screen. [aka slider, shelf, horizontal scroller]
version-history (pattern · collaborate) — Version history: A browsable record of past states of an artifact, with authorship, so a person can compare, restore or branch from an earlier version. [aka revision history, timeline of changes, checkpoints]
video-call (pattern · communicate) — Video call: Real-time audio and video among several participants, with shared content and side channels. [aka video meeting, conference call]
timeline-editor (pattern · create) — Timeline editor: Composing time-based media by arranging clips on tracks against a time axis. [aka non-linear editor, NLE, sequencer, arrangement view]
color-picker (component · enter-data) — Colour picker: A control for choosing a colour, by sight, by value or by name. [aka color picker, swatches, eyedropper]
date-picker (component · enter-data) — Date picker: A control for choosing a date, a time or a range of dates. [aka calendar picker, date range picker]
object-viewer-3d (pattern · explore-space) — 3D object viewer: A three-dimensional model presented for inspection — orbit, pan, zoom and sometimes explode or cross-section — to understand form, fit or configuration. [aka model viewer, 3D viewer, orbit viewer, product 3D]
availability-picker (pattern · schedule) — Availability picker: A surface for choosing a free time from offered or computed availability — for booking someone else, polling a group, or finding mutual free slots. [aka slot picker, booking calendar, find-a-time, scheduler]
gantt-timeline (pattern · schedule) — Gantt timeline: Tasks or phases as bars on a horizontal time axis, often with dependencies, progress and a hierarchical work breakdown beside the bars. [aka Gantt chart, project timeline, roadmap timeline, bar schedule]
recommendations (pattern · search) — Recommendations: Items proposed by the system from a person’s behaviour, context or the current item, rather than from a query. [aka recommended for you, related items, shelves]

data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## accordion — Accordion (component, archetype browse-collections)
Stacked sections whose headers expand to reveal their content in place.
Aliases: disclosure, collapsible sections, expander
Anatomy: Header (The always-visible label); Panel (The revealed content); Indicator (Chevron or plus)
Related — specializes: overview-detail | neighbors: tabs, tree-view
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Expansion policy [scope] — How many sections can be open?
  - policy (single-select: one id) — Open at once
      one-at-a-time: One at a time — Opening one closes the others (e.g. ESPN player stats)
      many-at-a-time: Many at a time — Sections open independently (e.g. weather.com hourly details)
      all-open-by-default: All open by default (e.g. Printable FAQs)
* Header content [content] — What does a closed section say about what is inside?
  - header (multi-select: list of ids) — Header content
      title-only: Title only (e.g. FAQ pages)
      title-plus-summary-value: Title plus summary value (e.g. Checkout order summary)
      status-indicator: Status indicator (e.g. Settings sections showing errors)
* Toggle [invocation] — How is a section opened?
  - toggle (multi-select: list of ids) — Toggle by
      header-click: Header click (e.g. Most accordions)
      indicator-only: Indicator only (e.g. Tree-like panels)
      expand-all-control: Expand all control (e.g. Documentation sites)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. WAI-ARIA accordion pattern)
* Memory [lifecycle] — Does it remember what was open?
  - memory (single-select: one id) — State memory
      resets: Resets (e.g. Most web pages)
      per-session: Per session (e.g. Single-page apps)
      persists: Persists (e.g. IDE side panels)

input.rationale: The Vercel hero has a 'Platform capabilities' list. Hovering an item expands its descriptive sentence in place and collapses the others. None of the existing toggle values (header-click, indicator-only, expand-all-control, keyboard) describes a section that opens on hover.

values.name: Hover
values.description: A section expands when the pointer rests on its header and collapses when the pointer moves to another one. This is common in minimalist marketing heroes.

label.notes: Near-monochrome Vercel/Geist look: off-white #fafafa page, near-black #171717 type and primary buttons, and only a hint of blue (the status dot and the Backends card corner). The hero is anchored by a huge solid black triangle centered between the left-aligned headline and a right-aligned capability list. Primary CTAs are fully rounded pills (black filled plus white with a hairline shadow ring), while nav buttons and cards use 6px radii. Customer showcases alternate headline alignment left/right and use greyscale, faded-out mock UIs of customer products (Notion AI chat, Zapier site, Mintlify docs), each with a two-tone quote ('Notion powers millions' dark, rest grey) and a 'Features' list. Much of the lower page (Mintlify mock, Recently shipped bento, final CTA, footer) did not render in the static capture because of scroll-reveal animations; it was verified on the live page. Footer: 12 link columns in a 6-col grid, 'New' pills, a mono 'ALL SYSTEMS NORMAL.' status line with a blue dot, a theme segmented switch, and a 'View as AI agent' button. The capture has no codebook entry for the customer logo strip (social proof). A proposal was filed for a hover toggle on accordion.
